title: Pop hits — the stories behind the videos

facts: "Rio" isn't about the Brazilian city — the name is a metaphor for America, the market Duran Duran were desperate to crack: "from the mountains in the north down to the Rio Grande."
The video was shot over three days in May 1982 off Antigua, aboard a 1936 wooden Fife yacht called the Eilean — later rescued and restored by an Italian watch company in 2009.
Keyboardist Nick Rhodes was seasick through much of the shoot: "I hate boats unless they're tied up and you're having cocktails on them."
During a break in filming, Simon Le Bon and John Taylor went for a swim and were hauled out of the water just as sharks closed in.
The crew ran out of film stock, so John Taylor's saxophone scene on the mountaintop was shot on a camera borrowed from a passing tourist.
"Rock DJ" was Robbie Williams' third UK No.1 and won British Single of the Year at the 2001 BRIT Awards.
The track is built on samples: Barry White's "It's Ecstasy When You Lay Down Next to Me," A Tribe Called Quest's "Can I Kick It?", and a line from Slick Rick & Doug E. Fresh's "La Di Da Di."
In the video Robbie strips naked to win a DJ's attention — and when that fails, he peels off his own skin and muscle until he's just a dancing skeleton.
The gory ending got the video cut or banned on most TV channels, and banned outright in the Dominican Republic over accusations of Satanism.
Lorde later said her 2021 single "Solar Power" was directly inspired by "Rock DJ."
Britney Spears — "Oops!... I Did It Again" (2000)
"Oops!... I Did It Again" was written and produced by Max Martin and Rami Yacoub as the lead single from Britney's second album (April 2000).
The entire video is set on Mars, directed by Nigel Dick, with Britney dancing on the red planet in a now-iconic red catsuit.
The catsuit was Britney's own idea — she told the director: "I want to be in a red jumpsuit... but there can't be any rockets."
The spoken bridge is a nod to Titanic: an astronaut hands Britney the "Heart of the Ocean" necklace that Rose threw into the sea.
The single hit No.1 in more than 20 countries and earned a 2001 Grammy nomination for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance.
